# Product of intervals, one-limb bounds

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/milestone1/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `interval_mul_1` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

An interval $Z = [z_l, z_u]$ that contains $x y$ for every $x \in X$, $y \in Y$, with $X = [x_l, x_u]$ and $Y = [y_l, y_u]$. An interval may be unbounded, and empty.

$$Z \supseteq \{\, x y : x \in X, y \in Y \,\}.$$

## C++

| Form | Operands | Result | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `X * Y` | `Interval<T, 1>`, `Interval<T, 1>` | `Interval<T, 1>` | rounds; not `constexpr`: its code is where `KAIRN_ENCLOSURE_CODE` puts it |
| `X *= Y` | `Interval<T, 1>`, `Interval<T, 1>` | `Interval<T, 1>` | rounds; not `constexpr`: its code is where `KAIRN_ENCLOSURE_CODE` puts it |

`T` is `float` or `double`; the operations are in namespace `kairn`, header `kairn/kairn.hpp`. The operators and functions also accept the marker `kairn::unverified` on an operand, which they need while the kernel is UNVERIFIED.

## Requires

- $X = [x_l, x_u]$ is a canonical interval: the empty set, $x_l = +\infty$ and $x_u = -\infty$, or a nonempty interval, neither bound a NaN, $x_l \le x_u$, $x_l < +\infty$, $x_u > -\infty$, each bound a number of `T` or an infinity; its members are the real numbers between its bounds.
- $Y = [y_l, y_u]$ is a canonical interval: the empty set, $y_l = +\infty$ and $y_u = -\infty$, or a nonempty interval, neither bound a NaN, $y_l \le y_u$, $y_l < +\infty$, $y_u > -\infty$, each bound a number of `T` or an infinity; its members are the real numbers between its bounds.

## Guarantees

For operands that satisfy the requirements, finite, infinite or NaN:

- **I1.** The result $Z = [z_l, z_u]$ is a canonical interval.
- **I2.** $Z$ is empty exactly when an operand is.
- **I3.** $Z$ contains $x y$ for every $x \in X$, $y \in Y$, unbounded operands included (their members are real numbers).
- **I4.** For nonempty $X$ and $Y$, where $\ell$ and $h$ are the greatest lower bound and the least upper bound of the exact range $\{\, x y : x \in X, y \in Y \,\}$, as extended real numbers: $z_l$ is $\mathrm{RD}(\ell)$ or at most 1 step of `T` below it, and $z_u$ is $\mathrm{RU}(h)$ or at most as many above it; exactly $\mathrm{RD}(\ell)$ and $\mathrm{RU}(h)$ when each product of a finite bound of $X$ and a finite bound of $Y$ is zero or at least $\eta/(2u^2)$ in magnitude.
- **I5.** For bounded $X$ and $Y$, $Z$ is bounded exactly when every member $z$ of the exact range satisfies $\lvert z\rvert \le \Omega$.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 1 bit, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the IEEE model, with signed zeros, infinities, NaN and overflow. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `interval_mul_1_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/IeeeInterval1.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/IeeeInterval1.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions interval_mul_1_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proof of `interval_mul_1_correct` depends on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** the least and the greatest of the directed products of the bounds (Milestone 2 listing). **License:** algorithm and proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/interval_mul_1.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/interval_mul_1.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal model (`proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).
It calls [`mul_dir_1`](mul_dir_1.md).

```
# The product of two intervals with one-limb bounds, without a branch (milestone2.md, "Interval
# kernels", "One limb"): the four products of bounds, each rounded down and up by mul_dir_1 (0
# times infinity is 0), the least of the four lower values and the greatest of the four upper ones;
# the empty set when an operand is empty. Each bound is the directed rounding of the bound of the
# exact range or one step beyond it, and the directed rounding when each of the four products of
# bounds is zero, infinite or at least P = 2^(2p-1) eta in magnitude. For every precision.

(d1, v1) = mul_dir_1(xl, yl)
(d2, v2) = mul_dir_1(xl, yu)
(d3, v3) = mul_dir_1(xu, yl)
(d4, v4) = mul_dir_1(xu, yu)
ma       = lt(d2, d1)
da       = select(ma, d2, d1)
mb       = lt(d4, d3)
db       = select(mb, d4, d3)
mc       = lt(db, da)
l        = select(mc, db, da)
na       = lt(v1, v2)
va       = select(na, v2, v1)
nb       = lt(v3, v4)
vb       = select(nb, v4, v3)
nc       = lt(va, vb)
h        = select(nc, vb, va)
nx       = lt(xl, const inf)
ny       = lt(yl, const inf)
ne       = and(nx, ny)
mi       = neg(const inf)
zl       = select(ne, l, const inf)
zu       = select(ne, h, mi)
```
